annotations.annotation_text: Page 197 opens Book 1, Chapter 8 ("Anna Livia Plurabelle") during the Age of Gods (closing) phase. This passage continues the two washerwomen gossiping on opposite banks of the darkening Liffey, 500+ river names woven into the text, metamorphosis into elm and stone, featuring ALP, the two washerwomen. The nocturnal dream-narrative layers Dublin topography, world mythology, and linguistic alchemy into polysemic prose.

annotations.annotation_text: Tavern/jury motif "bar" on page 197 ("Anna Livia Plurabelle"): the twelve customers drinking in HCE's Chapelizod pub represent public opinion, the Zodiac, and the Apostles within the two washerwomen gossiping on opposite banks of the darkening Liffey, 500+ river names woven into the text, metamorphosis into elm and stone. During this Age of Gods (closing) phase, they judge, condemn, and demand another round — the Greek chorus of middle-class Dublin gossip.
